title: ShakeMap shaking in 2015-2026 exceeded 2014 USGS hazard-model PGA levels at 0.25 of the expected rate in the conterminous US; unsampled M6.6+ events and map uncertainty explain much of the gap
abstract: Question: in a prospective window, did shaking in the conterminous United States exceed the PGA levels of the 2014 USGS National Seismic Hazard Model (NSHM, Vs30 760 m/s) at the model rate? Approach: for 2015-01-01 to 2026-11-01 (11.8 years) we used the ShakeMap median and uncertainty grids of 297 M4.5+ earthquakes, converted PGA to the model reference condition and summed exceedance probabilities over a 0.05-degree grid. The main test used 83 tectonic M4.7+ mainshocks and excluded induced-seismicity boxes. We split the expectation by magnitude with the model's own disaggregation at 120 random sites. Results: the observed exceedance count was 0.25-0.29 of the expected count for return periods of 50-2,475 years (475 years: 0.6% of the area exceeded against 2.5% expected; eight variants 0.19-0.40). All regions had a deficit (California 0.27, Intermountain West 0.29, central and eastern US 0.26, Pacific Northwest about 0). M6.6+ earthquakes supply 30-50% of the western 475-year expectation and are too rare to sample in 12 years. For the testable M<6.6 part, California gave 0.23 (475 years) and 0.47 (50 years) of the expectation (p<0.01), but 0.56 and 0.65 (p 0.07, 0.13) with a 1.4 times larger map standard deviation. In the Intermountain West, M4.6-5.6 events gave 0.01-0.20 in all variants, together with a 2015-2026 M5.0-5.6 mainshock rate of 0.30 of the 1932-2014 rate. A positive control found 6-16 times the long-term expectation in the induced boxes when induced events were kept. Limitations: ShakeMap tails away from stations, generic component and site conversions, ComCat magnitude mix, small disaggregation samples and a null that cannot represent unobserved large events. We do not conclude that the 2014 model overpredicts hazard.

Shading: range over eight sensitivity variants. Points with less than 30% defined area are omitted; values below 0.001 are drawn at 0.001. b) Ratio at the 475-yr level for each variant (colours as in a).

a, b) Observed / expected exceedances by magnitude class at the 475-yr and 50-yr levels; the expected count is split with the 2014.R2 disaggregation at random sites. Dots: main test; line end: map SD x 1.4. Grey band: the primary M<6.6 test. Zero values are drawn at 0.0015 and marked 0. c) Declustered M5+ mainshock rate 2015-2026 divided by the 1932-2014 rate, with 90% intervals and the 2015-2026 count.

a) 2014 NSHM PGA with a 475-yr return period (Vs30 760 m/s). b) Probability that this level was exceeded at least once in 2015-01 to 2026-10, from ShakeMap medians and uncertainty grids (main test), with mainshock epicentres (circles: tectonic; squares: induced boxes, not in the main test). The expected exceeded area is 2.5%; the observed is 0.6%.
